original_poem:
ਮਿੱਟੀ ਦੀ ਢੇਰੀ
ਮੇਰੀ ਨਮ ਭਿੱਜੀ ਮਿੱਟੀ ਨੂੰ
ਕਿੰਨਾ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਗੂੰਧਿਆ ਸੀ
ਇੱਕ ਘੜਾ ਬਣਾਇਆ ਸੀ
ਜੋ ਦੂਰ ਦੇ ਪਿੰਡਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਸੀ
ਪਰ ਮੇਰੇ ਹੀ ਝੋਨੇ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਪਾਣੀ ਲੈ ਕੇ।

ਫਿਰ ਇੱਕ ਦਿਨ ਘੜਾ ਟੁੱਟ ਗਿਆ
ਤੇ ਮੈਂ ਸਿਰਫ ਢੇਰੀ ਹੀ ਰਹਿ ਗਿਆ
ਮਿੱਟੀ ਦੀ ਢੇਰੀ।
translated_poem:
A Heap of Clay
My moist, wet clay
Was shaped so beautifully
Into a pitcher
That traveled to distant lands
But carried water from my own well.

One day, the pitcher broke
And I remained
Just a heap of clay.

stanzas.loss_note: ਝੋਨੇ (jhone) means a paddy/rice field or well-source rooted in the speaker's own land — translated as 'well' which loses the agricultural, soil-bound specificity central to the poem's mitti (clay/earth) imagery.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: the speaker's own pliable, fertile selfhood before being shaped by another's hands
the formed identity that served distant purposes while drawing from the speaker's own source

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: the collapse of the shaped identity that had given the speaker purpose and form
the speaker reduced to formless, purposeless origin after the loss of selfhood

cultural_entities.translation_note: Mitti in Punjabi carries the weight of ancestral soil, mortality, and belonging — 'clay' in the translation strips this layered cultural resonance.
Pindan (villages) in Punjabi poetry evokes the specific rural homeland lost to partition and migration — rendered as 'distant lands' which loses this rootedness.
